title: Thimble bug bento — morning triage
content:
Quick capture for the morning (keep concise)

Context:
- Intermittent p95 spikes (~200ms delta) on text-gen route since deploy v2024.11.05. Not steady — flares happen in bursts every ~30–90m. Reported by SLO alerts and live traffic.
- Hypothesis space: KV cache thrash + microbatch scheduling edge + a rare kernel selection path causing a fallback to slower op.

Observations from last night (11/11 22:00–02:00):
- Pattern: spike coincides with multi-tenant burst (10–30 concurrent short requests, ~<=80 tokens).
- When spike occurs, CPU load on control plane pod increases modestly; GPU utilization stays moderate.
- Eviction logs show small bursts of KV evictions at ~100ms before spike.
- Affected model: rdlv-small-7B-q4; fallback profile not triggered.
- No thermal events on GPU (checked nv-smi logs).

Immediate checks (do these first)
- Reproduce locally with the same short-request pattern (use traffic-replay script).
  - script: tools/traffic/replay-shortburst.sh --model rdlv-small-7B-q4 --concurrency 20 --burst-interval 45s --req-len 30
- Tail eviction + batching logs: kubectl -n infra logs -f svc-runtime-01 --since=10m | grep -E "evict|batch|kv-cache|batcher"
- Perf profile of a spike by sampling: perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 20; perf report (on host).

Notes from quick experiments:
- Replay with concurrency 20 reproduced a p95 bump (~+170ms) within 3 bursts.
- Turning off prefix caching (config override) eliminated the bump in replay — suggests prefix/KV interaction.
- Small change in batcher window (from 2ms to 1ms) reduced the probability of a spike in replay but increased avg token latency by ~6ms.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache eviction race: microbatching and cache eviction interact such that an in-flight request loses its KV page and forces re-computation of a chunk -> CPU costs + latency. Explains burstiness.
2) Kernel fallback: rare sequence lengths cause the runtime to pick an unoptimized matmul kernel (cuBLAS->fallback) for a tiny set of shapes when batcher groups heterogeneous lengths.
3) NUMA/CUDA pinning mismatch under small bursts causes host<->GPU skews leading to queuing on control path.

Data to collect next:
- Per-request KV hit/miss flag sampled in logs for a window around spikes (add ephemeral logging at trace level).
- Add a short metric: runtime.kv.evictions_per_min and runtime.kv.misses_per_req (sampled percentile).
- Trace of kernel selection: instrument path that chooses kernels and emit model+shape->kernel mapping for the burst window.

Actionable todo (priority ordered):
- [ ] Add ephemeral trace logs to batcher and kv-cache (PR branch: asha/trace-kv-evict-2024-11) — limit to 1% of requests to reduce noise. (owner: Asha; ETA: today EOD)
- [ ] Re-run replay with and without prefix caching, capture logs, and attach perf profile. (owner: Diego; ETA: today lunch)
- [ ] Experiment: force-use-optimized-kernel flag for rdlv-small-7B-q4 on canary to see if spikes disappear. If yes, create follow-up to adjust kernel heuristics. (owner: Priya; ETA: tomorrow morning)
- [ ] Run NUMA/cuda pinning checklist on affected host pool, compare to unaffected pool: sudo numactl --hardware; nvidia-smi topo --matrix. (owner: Asha; ETA: today)
- [ ] Add a lightweight metric for kv evictions; dashboard tile on Console for quick lookout. (owner: SRE/infra; contact: Diego)
- [ ] If replay consistently reproduces, schedule 30min deep-dive with Priya + Diego + runtime infra (tomorrow 10:30am).

Commands/quick snippets I used:
- replay: ./tools/traffic/replay-shortburst.sh --model rdlv-small-7B-q4 --concurrency 20 --burst-interval 45s --req-len 30 --trace-file /tmp/replay-trace.json
- tail logs: kubectl -n infra logs -f svc-runtime-01 --since=30m | grep -E "evict|kv-cache|batcher" -n --line-buffered
- perf: sudo perf record -F 99 -p $(pgrep runtime-service) -g -- sleep 20; sudo perf report --children
- check topo: sudo nvidia-smi topo --matrix; sudo lscpu | sed -n '1,12p'

Quick dump of a sample trace (sanitized):
TS 2024-11-11T22:03:12Z | req_id b1f3 | batch_id 987 | kv_hit false | evict_trigger true | kernel_choice matmul_fallback_v2 | latency 312ms
TS 2024-11-11T22:03:12Z | req_id b1f4 | batch_id 987 | kv_hit false | evict_trigger true | kernel_choice matmul_fast_v1 | latency 138ms
(interesting: same batch, different kernel picks)

Open questions / thinking aloud:
- Why would two requests in same batch pick different kernels? Batcher shape grouping should be deterministic. Could there be a race where cache state influences kernel heuristics?
- If eviction is happening mid-batch, we should see a correlation between evict logs and kernel_fallback logs. Need to capture both in same trace.
- If forcing kernel eliminates problem, we need to understand long-term perf/cost tradeoffs (fallback may be slower but more numerically stable?).

Meeting prep (tomorrow deep dive):
- Bring: replay logs, two perf profiles (with/without prefix cache), batcher trace (per-batch shapes), host NUMA topo.
- Goal: pin root cause to either cache eviction or kernel selection; decide mitigation (short-term patch + long-term fix).

Notes to self: keep trace sampling low; do not enable heavy trace on prod without SRE guard. If we need more signal, run canary with 5% traffic and full traces.

Random tangents / ideas (capture quickly):
- Try a tiny experiment: decouple prefix cache eviction TTL on canary (e.g., 10s -> 60s) to see effect on spike frequency. Easy rollback.
- Consider a fast-path that pins kernel choice per-model at startup instead of per-batch if variance continues.

End note: prioritize reproducible replay + combined trace of batcher+kv+kernel-selection. If we can reproduce reliably, we can test mitigations quickly.

-- Asha
